followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain Narva 2/Parusinka’s reported closure on 28 November 2022 and its distinct parent. Narva 1 remains a separate crossing. The affected cohort is pedestrians eligible to use Narva 2; the main post was an alternative. No blanket Estonia–Russia or all-Narva closure is implied. The 2022 implementation report and 3 June 2026 ministerial account support a qualified censored 1,283-day lower bound. No reopening or evidence beyond that last confirmation is asserted. Staff/facility consolidation and reconstruction support Administration coding. The initiating minister expressly rejects security as the original closure rationale. The later ERR account was freshly inspected; the earlier ministry/order/implementation passages were reused. The later article’s French-citizen correction does not change the closure claim or create a new confirmation date. The Narva 2 pedestrian bridge remains unlocated. Its identity is kept distinct from Narva 1, rail infrastructure and national outlines.
